name: BaroEase
tagline: Migraine tracker with barometric pressure alerts. Your health data lives on your device; an account is optional.
overview: This Privacy Policy describes how {{app}} handles information when you use the app. It applies to every version of {{app}} distributed by {{publisher}} on the app stores listed above.

{{app}} is a migraine tracker for people whose attacks may be linked to barometric-pressure changes. It is built local-first: your health data is stored on your device, an account is optional, and logging an attack works with no network at all. The sections below set out exactly what is handled, why it is needed, and how you can have it removed.
The data controller for {{app}} is Dam Hong Duc, Ho Chi Minh City, Viet Nam, reachable at {{email}}.
If anything here is unclear, email {{email}} before you continue using the app.
summary: Your attacks, medications and notes are stored on your device. Without an account, we never receive them.
Signing in is optional and turns on encrypted cross-device sync. The key is held by our backend, so this is not end-to-end encryption.

Apple Health sleep and your menstrual cycle are read on-device only and are never uploaded. Your step count is read the same way, but the figure for the day of an attack is saved with that attack, and syncs with it if you are signed in.
Location is only requested While Using the app and at reduced accuracy, stored as a ~5 km area, never as coordinates.
We do not track you. No ad network, no attribution SDK, no advertising identifier, nothing shared with a data broker.

Weather snapshot attached to each attack
Home screen widget — this week's attack count and the latest pressure reading, in a container shared between the app and the widget

Account identifier and last-changed timestamp, stored unencrypted alongside each payload

Decide when a pressure alert is warranted and deliver it to your device. Stored against a random device identifier when you have no account.
Authenticate you and show you which account you are signed in to. Only collected if you choose to sign in with Google or Apple.

Identify and fix crashes and performance problems. Tagged with your opaque account identifier while you are signed in. Always on — there is no in-app switch yet; write to us and we will stop and erase yours.

sections.title: Local-first, account optional
body: {{app}} stores your migraine attacks, symptoms, triggers, notes, medications, reminders and notification history on your device. The app is fully usable with no account and no internet connection — logging an attack works entirely offline.
Signing in is optional and costs you nothing if you skip it. The only thing an account adds is cross-device sync.

sections.title: Sync is encrypted, but not end-to-end
body: Signing in turns on cross-device sync. There is no separate switch — the sign-in screen tells you this before you sign in. Your attacks, medications, reminders and notification history are then uploaded as encrypted payloads and pulled down on your other devices. Your on-device copy always remains the source of truth.
Two things travel with each record in readable form, because sync cannot work without them: which account owns it, and when it was last changed. Neither says anything about what is in the record.

The encryption key for your account is generated and held by our backend, so that a new device of yours can be given it after you sign in. That means Google's infrastructure, which hosts our backend, is technically able to decrypt these payloads. We do not read them and nothing in the app is designed to — but we will not tell you that only you can read them, because that would not be true.
Exports never sync. They stay on the device that made them.

sections.title: Apple Health
body: If you grant permission, {{app}} reads your sleep, your step count and your menstrual cycle from Apple Health, read-only, to look for a correlation with your attacks. These are three separate permissions with three separate switches — allowing one does not allow the others.

The analysis runs on your device and we never write to Apple Health. Sleep never leaves your device. Your step count does, in one narrow way: when you log an attack, {{app}} records how many steps you had taken that day up to that moment and saves the number with the attack, because how active you were before an attack is part of the record a doctor reads. It travels with that attack — into your export, your doctor report, and your encrypted sync if you are signed in. Nothing else from Apple Health is stored or uploaded, and you can revoke access at any time in the iOS Health settings.

sections.title: How weather reaches you
body: Weather comes from Apple WeatherKit, and {{app}} never calls it directly: the app asks our backend, and our backend asks Apple.

The app sends its reduced-accuracy position to our weather function, which rounds it to a ~11 km cell before anything else happens. What reaches Apple is the centre of that cell, never where you are, and the forecast is cached against that cell for an hour so everyone in it shares one lookup. That cache holds weather, not people — no account identifier, no device identifier, no health data.

The place name on the weather card is resolved by your device's own geocoder (Apple on iOS) from the same reduced-accuracy position. That lookup goes from your phone to the platform and never through us.

sections.title: What our App Store privacy labels say
body: Apple asks every developer to declare, on the App Store product page, what an app collects, whether it is linked to your identity, and whether it is used to track you. Below is exactly what {{app}} declares, so you can hold the labels and this policy against each other and see that they agree.

“Tracking” has a specific meaning in Apple's rules: linking data from this app with third-party data for advertising or advertising measurement, or sharing it with a data broker. {{app}} does none of that — there is no ad network, no attribution SDK, no advertising identifier is read, and nothing is sold or handed to a data broker. Every item below is declared as not used for tracking, and the app contains no App Tracking Transparency prompt because there is nothing to ask permission for.

Your sleep is not declared at all, because it never leaves your device. Fitness is declared, because the step count for the day of an attack is saved with that attack. Health is declared, because your attack log syncs to our backend once you sign in.
list: Name — App Functionality, linked to you. From the account you sign in with.
Email address — App Functionality, linked to you. From the account you sign in with.
Health — App Functionality, linked to you. Your synced attack log, medications and reminders.
Coarse location — App Functionality, linked to you. A ~5 km area, never coordinates.
User ID — App Functionality, linked to you. The opaque account identifier.
Device ID — App Functionality, linked to you. The push token that delivers pressure alerts.
Purchase history — App Functionality, linked to you. Which subscription you hold, via RevenueCat.
Product interaction — Analytics, linked to you. Which screens and features get used.
Crash data — App Functionality, linked to you. Crashes and non-fatal errors.
Fitness — App Functionality, linked to you. The step count saved with an attack.

sections.title: Sharing an attack
body: From an attack's detail screen you can share it as an image — to a partner, a family member, or anyone else you choose. It carries when the attack started, how intense it was, how long it lasted, and where on your head it hurt.

It never carries your notes, your symptoms, your triggers, the medication you took, or your location. You see the exact image before you send it, because what gets shared is the preview you are looking at.

The image goes only where you send it: it is handed to the iOS share sheet and reaches the app you pick. It is never uploaded to us, we never see it, and it never reaches our backend. The file is written to the app's temporary storage so the share sheet can read it, and “Delete all data” clears it along with everything else.

sections.title: Exporting and deleting your data
body: {{app}} gives you two destructive actions, deliberately kept separate.
list: Export everything — Settings → Export data, as JSON, CSV or a PDF doctor report. The in-app export is a Premium feature; without Premium, write to us and we will send you your data free of charge. Past exports are kept in the app so you can re-share them, and are full copies of your data.

Delete all data — Settings → Delete all data. Wipes the local database, those export files, any shared attack image and the home screen widget's shared container, deletes your synced records and backend alert record, and gives up your push token, coarse location and threshold. Your account stays, so your subscription binding survives.
Delete your account — Account screen → Delete account. The whole teardown: synced records, account record, encryption key, then the login itself.
Neither action cancels your subscription. That lives in the App Store and only you can cancel it there.

sections.title: Children's privacy
body: {{app}} is not directed at children under 16 and we do not knowingly collect personal information from them. If you believe a child has provided us with personal information, contact {{email}} and we will delete it.

sections.title: Medical disclaimer
body: {{app}} is a self-tracking tool. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. It does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any condition. Always consult a qualified clinician about your health.
